newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes to support won.

text.p: South Korea's central Bank of Korea (BOK) intervened in mid-morning trading on Wednesday to boost the won against the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
They said the BOK sold dollars at around the 830.30 level.
"It looks like the central bank began to sell dollars when the won fell to a new six-year low of 830.30," said a dealer with a domestic bank.
The level is the lowest for the won since South Korea introduced a market average system in March 1990.
Following the BOK intervention, the won was trading at 829.50 after opening at 829.70.
The won previously hit a six-year low of 830.00 on September 16, the dealers said.
They said they expected the currency to move between 827.00 and 830.00 in the afternoon.
